ordered_observations.uncertainty: No audio feedback confirms the actual moment of key presses; only the delayed verbal praise indicates success.

ordered_observations.threat_origin: Voice states at 53.5s that 'up is where the problems are' and mentions threading the gem between bullets (38.2s).

ordered_observations.goal_resource_change: Tutorial advances from focus practice to weapon firing instruction.
ordered_observations.uncertainty: Whether the player actually fired weapons after 50.4s cannot be determined because there are no distinct gunfire sound effects over the music.

simultaneous_information.competition: Continuous synth melody and percussion play underneath the tutorial voice throughout the clip.
simultaneous_information.consequence: Speech remains highly intelligible, though subtle mechanical/action SFX (if any exist) are either absent or masked by the music.

clips.rating_evidence: The single tutorial voice is well-paced and clearly explains mechanics, hitboxes, and threat direction ('up is where the problems are') without overlapping speech. However, cause attribution relies entirely on delayed verbal confirmation because player actions (moving, focusing, firing) lack distinct non-verbal sound effects.
uncertainties: 0.0s: First word is clipped ('...get from one place to another').
44.0s-48.5s and 55.0s-57.6s: Unclear if any player action SFX (focus hum or bullet firing) are occurring during the musical interludes.
clips.minimal_fix: Add distinct, audible sound effects for movement, focus activation, and weapon firing so action-response feedback does not rely solely on delayed voiceover confirmation.

cross_clip_summary: Both clips are audio-only ablations with blank video (text_legibility is null). Intelligibility is governed by voice queuing and non-verbal SFX: Sequence G is easy to follow because a single voice speaks clearly over background music, whereas Sequence C suffers from severe speech-on-speech masking (12.1s and 20.5s) where simultaneous voices obscure critical threat and rule-of-engagement details. Neither clip provides clear non-verbal audio cues for player actions or incoming threats prior to voiceover commentary.
